Subject: MAP Draft — Data handling & compliance milestones

Hi Emily — great conversation today. Thanks for taking the time to walk through AcroSoft's integration and compliance concerns. Per our call, I pulled together a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the data handling & compliance milestone so your legal and security teams have a clear roadmap.

High-level recap (action items follow):
- Redwood can support PHI-aware routing to private deployments (VPC) and configurable retention policies per customer.
- We maintain audit logs and exportable audit trails; SOC 2 report and summary attached.
- Key open items: exact retention windows for PHI, required granularity of audit trails, and whether De-identified derivatives are acceptable for analytics.

Draft MAP milestone: Data handling & compliance (proposed)
1) Define Data Classification & Acceptable Use (Owner: AcroSoft legal) — Target: 2026-06-24
   - Inputs: list of PII/PHI elements, retention policy ranges
   - Dependencies: legal signoff, definition of data flows
2) Technical Controls & Deployment Mode (Owner: Redwood infra lead / Rishi) — Target: 2026-06-28
   - Options: Hosted (not for PHI), Dedicated reserved capacity, Private VPC/on-prem
   - Deliverables: architecture diagram, encryption-at-rest/in-transit details, KMS integration notes
3) Logging & Audit Trail Specification (Owner: AcroSoft security / Redwood) — Target: 2026-06-30
   - Items: event types to log, retention window, export format (CSV/JSON), SIEM integration points (Splunk/Datadog)
4) Retention & Deletion Process (Owner: AcroSoft legal & Redwood) — Target: 2026-07-05
   - Items: retention schedules, deletion SLA, proof-of-deletion artifacts
5) Formal Security Questionnaire & Evidence Package (Owner: AcroSoft / Redwood) — Target: 2026-07-08
   - Deliverables: completed questionnaire, SOC2 summary, pen test report (if requested)

Attachments: acrosoft_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones column), redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (SOC 2 overview)

Next steps:
- Emily / Paul: review the Data Classification & retention targets and confirm owners by 6/18.
- Rishi / Neha: I’ll sync with you to prepare the architecture diagram and the SOC2 one-pager.

If this looks good I can update the MAP with any owner/target adjustments and send a version for your legal review.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear MAP, this is exactly what our legal/security folks wanted to see. A couple of clarifying questions before we confirm owners: 

1) PHI retention windows — we have two classes: (a) Clinical encounter data (retain 7 years), (b) De-identified analytics (retain 2 years). Can Redwood support per-class retention rules and automated purging with proof-of-deletion?

2) Audit trail granularity — our auditors require user-level event logs (who, what, when, request/response IDs) for any access to PHI. Would Redwood provide exportable logs and a mechanism to ship to our Splunk instance?

Adding Paul from IT security to confirm timing expectations. Also looping in Legal if we need to capture specific contractual language.

Marissa / Neha — quick internal note with suggested answers to Emily's questions so we can reply with specifics:

- Retention per-class: yes — our platform supports configurable retention policies at the dataset/tenant level. For PHI we recommend Private VPC or Dedicated (not Hosted). Automatic purge with an append-only proof-of-deletion record can be provided; we generate deletion manifests that include object keys and timestamp.

- Audit logs: we capture request-level metadata (request id, user/service principal, timestamp, model invoked, token counts). We can stream logs to customer SIEM via secure forwarder (TLS) or S3 export. We should note limits: raw model output is not included in the standard logs unless the customer opts into full request logging — that can be enabled for PHI workflows with agreed retention.

- Suggested owner mapping for reply: Rishi -> Technical Controls & Deployment Mode; Neha -> Logging & Audit Trail spec (she owns our observability integrations). I'll draft the architecture diagram and sample retention policy tonight.

Rishi
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Hi Emily / Paul — thanks for the quick questions. Below are concrete responses and an updated MAP attachment (acrosoft_MAP_v1.xlsx -> acrosoft_MAP_v1.1.xlsx). I also attached our SOC 2 summary again for your legal team.

Responses to your questions:
1) Retention per-class — Confirmed. Redwood supports per-class retention rules at tenant/dataset level. For PHI (clinical encounter data) we recommend Private VPC or Dedicated Dedicated capacity; automatic purging is supported and we produce a deletion manifest (object ids + timestamps). We can provide a signed attestation of deletion upon request.

2) Audit trail granularity — We provide request-level logs with request_id, caller identity, timestamp, model identifier, and action. Full request/response bodies are off by default; they can be enabled for PHI workflows under a documented retention policy. Logs can be exported in JSONL or CSV and shipped to S3 or pushed to Splunk/Datadog via our forwarder.

Updated MAP (highlights):
- Data Classification & Acceptable Use — Owner: AcroSoft Legal — Target: 2026-06-24 (action: confirm PHI classes)
- Technical Controls & Deployment Mode — Owner: Rishi Malhotra (Redwood) — Target: 2026-06-28 (action: architecture diagram, KMS notes)
- Logging & Audit Trail Specification — Owner: Neha Kapoor (Redwood) + AcroSoft Security — Target: 2026-06-30 (action: sample log schema + exporter config)
- Retention & Deletion Process — Owner: AcroSoft Legal & Redwood (Neha) — Target: 2026-07-05 (action: retention table + deletion SLA)
- Security Questionnaire & Evidence — Owner: AcroSoft / Redwood — Target: 2026-07-08 (action: upload completed questionnaire)

Dependencies & notes:
- PHI work will require Private VPC or Dedicated capacity and a commercial agreement covering data residency and KMS integration.
- If AcroSoft requires full request/response logging for PHI, we need to scope storage and retention costs as a line item in the deal (we'll provide an estimate).

Attachments: acrosoft_MAP_v1.1.xlsx, redwood_soc2_summary.pdf

Next steps:
- Emily/Paul: confirm owners & retention classes by 6/18 so we can lock targets.
- Rishi/Neha: I'll schedule a short architecture sync for 6/19 to review diagram & exporter config.

Thanks — I’ll update the MAP in Drive after we confirm owners.

Best,
Marissa
